T01.what: The orbit rings are strengthened so they build a visible glow where orbits cluster, and a sentence is added to the side text explaining that the centre stays dark (only 167 planets under a day).

T02.what: Vertical position within each year's stratum changes from loose size-based settling to strict grading by size rank (small on top, large at the bottom), so each layer now reads as a sorted sediment with a bright floor of giants; the subtitle is rewritten to match.

T03.what: Stratum thickness changes from purely proportional to a fixed floor plus proportional, so every year (including empty or one-planet years like 1993, 1995, 1997) gets its own labelled row and the early years spread out down the page.

T04.what: The outer rim becomes a calendar of alternating-tone segments, one per discovery year with labels and counts for 2014/2016/2021, and the planets with unknown period move from outside the rim to just inside it.

T05.what: The 28 planets with no known distance become hollow rings just outside the last circle instead of solid dots, and a legend line is added explaining them.

T06.what: Ticks with labels (1,000th to 6,000th) are added around the rim for every thousandth planet, plus a paragraph in the side text explaining the counter.

T07.what: Full bright lines of sight are drawn from the Sun to the four labelled landmark planets, and the side text mentions them.

T08.what: Dots are drawn in layers with the rare-method planets on top and given a thin dark edge, so a few microlensing, imaging and other-method dots that were buried under transit and radial-velocity dots become visible; the change is subtle.

T09.what: Four labelled landmark planets are added (first confirmed, 51 Peg b, Proxima Cen b, SWEEPS-11 b), along with a dot-size key in the side panel.

T10.what: The side text gains concrete counts (5,439 of 6,097, 89%, faster than Earth; 2,937 under ten days), and the dial shifts slightly left.

T11.what: Faint shaded fans are added from the centre to the rim for the 2014 and 2016 arcs, and the text is changed to call them shaded fans.

T12.what: Brightness becomes a new encoding for distance (near planets bright, far ones dim), so the dense Kepler strata now read dim, and a near/far key is added at the bottom left.

T13.what: A small size key (Earth-size floats / Jupiter-size sinks) is added at the bottom left, and the 1992 annotation gets a leader line and longer wording, along with small label rewordings.

T14.what: The subtitle and annotations are tightened and reworded (with a short 'Brighter means nearer' added) while the plot itself stays unchanged.

T15.what: The boxed legend that sat over the top-right of the plot is moved into a single unboxed row above the chart, which uncovers the long-period imaging and radial-velocity planets it was hiding; the plot is slightly re-scaled.

T16.what: The side text is shortened into two tighter paragraphs, and the colliding rim labels (2019 and the 4,000th tick, among others) are separated, with no change to the dial.
